chronology_preview.narrative_summary: 2020 was the year of the great retreat and fortification for Julius. The pandemic lockdown provided an unexpected crucible for his ambition. He turned his small apartment into a training ground, using mannequin heads and online tutorials to obsessively hone his technical skills. This period of intense isolation wasn't lonely; it was a focused, almost monastic dedication to building a professional identity so strong it could withstand any future social insecurity.

events.description: Upon the city-wide lockdown, Julius invests a significant portion of his meager savings into professional-grade tools: a set of Japanese shears, a high-end blow dryer, and a collection of mannequin heads. He sets up a rigid daily schedule of 8 hours of practice, treating his living room like a salon.
events.psychological_note: This is an act of self-soothing through control. The world outside is chaotic and uncertain, but the geometry of a haircut is logical and precise. He is building his fortress of competence brick by brick.

events.description: Julius starts a private, password-protected Instagram account dedicated solely to macro shots of his practice haircuts. He focuses on documenting perfect lines, seamless layers, and color theory, using a sterile, academic aesthetic. He doesn't follow anyone back.
events.psychological_note: This is the creation of a digital moat. It allows him to engage with his craft and a hypothetical audience without the vulnerability of real-time interaction or judgment. It's a gallery, not a conversation.
